title: Set and uniqueness
learningObjectives: Explain set and uniqueness and use JavaScript collections and iteration safely.

understand.concept: Set stores unique values and iterates them in insertion order. Adding a value already present does not create a duplicate. Set uses SameValueZero equality semantics for membership, which treats NaN as equal to itself.
understand.whyItMatters: Set provides a direct way to deduplicate primitive values and check membership. Object values are unique by reference identity, not by matching object contents.
understand.analogy: A Set is a collection that keeps one entry for each distinct value.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; collection identity, iteration, and binary storage follow JavaScript specification rules.

explain.narrative: Converting the array to a Set removes repeated string values; spreading converts the set back into an array.

practise.guidedTask: Deduplicate a list of tags. Then add two separate object literals with the same fields and explain why both remain in the Set.
practise.independentTask: Choose an appropriate collection or iteration technique for a small data task. Test duplicates, ordering, identity, and copying behaviour.

questions.prompt: Why can two different object literals with identical properties both exist in a Set?
questions.explanation: Set compares objects by reference identity rather than deep property equality.
